intendedUse: Draft tier-1 billing responses for review before sending.
workflowBoundary: Incoming tier-1 billing ticket and supplied account context through draft generation, verification, authorised send decision, and delivery to the customer.
workflowCompletion: The workflow is complete when an authorised support agent has sent or rejected/escalated the response and the action is recorded.
downstreamHandoffs: Escalation to the existing support workflow when the request is unsupported or uncertain
movedBottleneck: If draft generation becomes faster, review queue time and account-data verification may become the binding constraints.
unhappyPath: Missing or contradictory account data, unsupported ticket categories, low-confidence drafts, or failed downstream delivery must escalate to the existing support process rather than silently completing.

actors.role: Draft a proposed response from supplied ticket and account context.
Authorised support agent decides whether to send, edit, or reject the draft.

assurance: Escalation on low confidence or unsupported request
authority: The AI may draft but may not send. The authorised support agent controls external communication.
accountability: Support Team Lead owns the workflow, evaluation criteria, and corrective action.
demonstrated: Drafts can be generated from supplied ticket and account context and evaluated against the named acceptance criteria.
inferredOrAssumed: Unseen ticket categories may contain requirements outside the evaluation set.
knownLimitations: Requests outside the tested billing categories are out of scope
acceptanceCriteria: Balance figures agree with supplied account data
Unsupported requests escalate instead of inventing policy
nextEvidence: Run a 100-case shadow evaluation on fresh tickets before widening the intended use.
stopRule: Do not permit reliance outside the tested billing categories; stop the trial if the defined account-data error threshold is exceeded.
notes: Illustrative adopter record. Replace thresholds and evidence references with the organisation's own decision criteria.
